html:
The Tatuyo, who call themselves Umurecoómajá, are a small people of the Pirá Paraná and upper Vaupés area in southeastern Colombia. They speak one of the Tucanoan languages.

Like other peoples of the Vaupés, such as the Carapana and Taiwano, they live in riverside longhouses, grow bitter manioc and fish. Men marry women from other language groups, so households mix several languages. Rubber traders and later missions reached the region in the late 1800s and 1900s. Neighbours: Yurutí.
